sections.html:
Polk County is Iowa's most populous county, with 492,401 residents in the 2020 census and an estimated 516,546 in 2025. Des Moines is the county seat, the state capital and the largest city in Iowa. The six-county Des Moines metro held 779,048 people in 2024. Insurance and finance anchor the job base.

One large city sits inside a ring of suburbs, and each suburb has its own city services and school district. Windsor Heights, Clive, Waukee and Altoona round out the metro.

Parts of Des Moines south of County Line Road extend into Warren County, so a Des Moines mailing address does not prove Polk County sends the bill. Before you ask anyone for a payoff, confirm which county's treasurer holds the parcel.

Owners near the Des Moines and Raccoon rivers should also have flood zone and insurance information ready for a buyer. Major floods hit downtown in 1993 and 2008, and a buyer's lender is likely to ask about both the zone and your insurance history.

Two county offices split the work. The Polk County Assessor values property and the Polk County Treasurer collects the tax. The Assessor is at 111 Court Avenue, Room 195, Des Moines, IA 50309, phone (515) 286-3014.

The Treasurer's office is open 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. for all services, and payment options remain available when it is closed. It also administers the Senior and Disabled Property Tax Credit for owners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, and who meet the yearly income limits.

Polk follows the state two-year cycle. Values are updated in odd-numbered years and generally left alone in even-numbered years, except for new construction, demolition or other changes to a specific property. When a value changes, notices go out before April 1.

Your protest must be written and signed, filed between April 2 and April 30, with a separate form for each parcel. A deadline that falls on a weekend moves to the next business day.

  • An informal review with the Assessor is available April 2 through April 25.
  • A signed agreement with the Assessor makes a formal protest unnecessary.
  • Strong evidence includes an appraisal, recent sales, or three to five comparable sales.
  • Argue the value as of the January 1 assessment date.

There are separate forms for residential, commercial and agricultural property. Commercial owners may offer three years of operating statements and a current rent roll, though that is optional. The allowed grounds are in Iowa Code 441.37, and the Assessor summary walks through the steps.

sections.h2: Preparing a protest, step by step
sections.html:
Start in January with the date in mind: the value being tested is the one as of January 1. When your notice arrives before April 1, compare the new figure with last year's. If it rose, line up evidence before you call anyone. An appraisal is the strongest single piece, and three to five comparable sales is the usual alternative. Write down the parcel number, because each parcel needs its own form.

Next, try the informal route. Between April 2 and April 25 you can ask the Assessor to look at your numbers. If the two of you agree, a signed agreement ends the matter, with no hearing at all. If you do not agree, file the formal protest before April 30 and ask for an oral hearing in the same filing, since the board only grants one when you request it up front.

Expect the board to meet in May and normally finish by May 31. If you asked for an oral hearing when you filed, you get one. A written decision with reasons follows by mail.

An owner who loses can go to the Property Assessment Appeal Board or district court, with 20 days counted from adjournment or May 31, whichever is later. In odd years the board may also hold a special session from October 10 to November 15, where the only ground is that a state equalization order would push the value above actual value (see the Department of Revenue).

sections.h2: Delinquency dates and the tax sale
sections.html:
The first half is delinquent October 1 and the second April 1. Interest is one and one-half percent a month, rounded to the nearest dollar with a $1 floor (Iowa Code 445.39). Ask the Treasurer to confirm the exact due dates for your parcel.

Delinquent parcels go to the annual sale, held by default on the third Monday in June, and bidding has been online in recent years. The property list is published in the newspaper in early June. An owner can redeem by paying the sale price, fees and 2% monthly interest counted from the month of sale (Iowa Code 447.1).

sections.h2: What happens to tax when you sell
sections.html:
A declaration of value travels with the deed to the recorder, who passes it to the assessor. Transfer tax is 80 cents per $500 above the first $500 (Iowa Code 428A.1). The statute never says which side pays, so your contract settles it.

Property tax is a lien on the parcel, ahead of every claimant except the state. On the homestead credit, a buyer of a house sold before July 1 must file by July 1. A sale on or after July 1 keeps the credit with the property that year (rule 701-110.1).

  • Order a payoff from the Treasurer for each parcel.
  • Confirm which county bills a parcel near County Line Road.
  • Ask the closing agent who covers the second-half tax and transfer tax.

Start by getting the payoff in writing from the Treasurer, then compare it with what the house should sell for. A traditional listing in a metro this size can work well when a house is in good shape, but it means prep, showings and waiting on a buyer's loan. If the house needs work, or the June sale date is close, an as-is cash sale shortens the timeline. The unpaid taxes are paid from the price at closing either way.

Gather the latest tax statement, the Assessor's parcel record and any repair or flood records before you talk to a buyer. That keeps surprises off the closing table.

faqs.q: What is the Polk County Assessor's address?
faqs.a: 111 Court Avenue, Room 195, Des Moines, IA 50309. The phone number is (515) 286-3014.

faqs.q: When can I protest my Polk County property tax assessment?
faqs.a: From April 2 through April 30. A separate signed form is needed for each parcel, and a weekend deadline moves to the next business day.

faqs.q: How often are Polk County values updated?
faqs.a: Every two years, in odd-numbered years, with few changes in even years beyond new construction, demolition or property-specific changes.

faqs.q: Can part of Des Moines be taxed by Warren County?
faqs.a: Yes. Parts of Des Moines south of County Line Road extend into Warren County, so ask which county's treasurer bills your parcel.

faqs.q: What interest applies to late Iowa property tax?
faqs.a: One and one-half percent per month, rounded to the nearest whole dollar with a $1 minimum. A fraction of a month counts as a full month.
